facts.label: Tutankhamun's tomb
facts.fact: In 1922 Howard Carter broke into the near-intact tomb of the minor pharaoh Tutankhamun — asked what he saw, he answered, "wonderful things."

facts.label: Coming Forth by Day
facts.fact: The funerary spellbook we call the Book of the Dead bore an Egyptian name closer to The Book of Coming Forth by Day.

facts.label: The Standard of Ur
facts.fact: The inlaid panel called the Standard of Ur gives a vivid picture of Early Dynastic kingship and its beliefs about the beyond.

facts.label: The Ziggurat of Ur
facts.fact: The great stepped platform-tower crowning a Mesopotamian city has its most famous survivor in the ziggurat of Ur.

facts.label: Writing began as accounting
facts.fact: The earliest cuneiform tablets are accounts — measures of barley, heads of livestock, rations of beer — before writing ever recorded a myth.

facts.label: The Indus seal
facts.fact: At Mohenjo-daro excavators turned up a small steatite seal showing a seated figure — famous but still undeciphered.

facts.label: The Great Bath
facts.fact: Mohenjo-daro's most striking structure is the Great Bath, a watertight sunken tank of fitted brick sealed with bitumen.

facts.label: The Behistun inscription
facts.fact: At Behistun, Darius carved his victories into living rock and credited Ahura Mazda — one of the most important royal inscriptions of the ancient world.
